Subject: SIG questionnaire intake + ask for artifact extraction playbook

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this on. We're the procurement/security team at Stellarus and we've received your standard SIG request via the portal. Our InfoSec reviewer asked whether you can provide an 'artifact extraction playbook' — basically a short runbook that maps SIG control IDs to the specific artifacts (logs, configs, policies) and where we'll be able to retrieve them.

Two asks to start: (1) can you share a one-page playbook and an estimated timeline to produce the initial evidence packet for a SIG Full review? (2) we have an accelerated procurement window and would like to know what can be delivered within 10 business days (SOC 2 artifacts + crypto/key provenance).

Attaching the questionnaire we uploaded for context (Stellarus_SIG_Questionnaire_2028.xlsx).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Regards,
Daniel Wu
Head of Procurement, Stellarus
procure@stellarus.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire intake + ask for artifact extraction playbook

Hi Daniel — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Short answers up front: we can produce an artifact extraction playbook + an initial SOC 2 evidence bundle. Below is the plan and a proposed timeline.

Plan (high level):
- Day 0: Intake & mapping — we map the SIG IDs to our control assertions and enumerate available artifacts.
- Day 1–3: Collect copies of non-sensitive artifacts (policies, runbooks, config snippets).
- Day 4–7: Compile logs and trace artifacts (retention, access logs); mask or redact where required.
- Day 8–10: Crypto/key provenance deliverable and final packaging; produce a consolidation index (CSV) that maps control -> artifact -> location.

Deliverables (what you'll get):
- Artifact extraction playbook (PDF) — control mapping, collector contacts, and evidence locations.
- Initial SOC 2 evidence bundle (zipped index pointing to S3 objects).
- Key provenance statement (PDF) — high-level KMS/HSM flow and signing key ownership.

Constraints / notes:
- We do not share raw private keys; we provide key provenance and KMS configuration exports.
- For any tenant-specific telemetry that contains PII, we'll provide redacted extracts or aggregated summaries.

Next steps: I'll (Jasmine) coordinate with Neha (security ops) to spin up the artifact collection. Karthik — can you own the log pulls and retention evidence?

If that timeline works, we'll target a 10-business-day delivery for the initial packet and keep you updated via the S3 staging folder. I'll attach our playbook draft now.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer — Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood_sig_extraction_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF stub, 420 KB)

Hi Daniel — thanks for the questions. Quick responses below and actions.

1) Key provenance: Redwood uses Redwood-managed KMS for platform-level signing keys and supports optional customer-managed keys (CMK) for isolated private deployments. For hosted customers (like your initial PO scenario), model artifact signing is Redwood-managed; we will provide a key provenance statement that shows KMS ARNs, rotation windows, and signing policy excerpts. We will not disclose secret key material. See attached redwood_key_provenance_statement.pdf for the standard language.

2) Third-party dependencies: monitoring is provided by a mix of in-house agents plus a managed observability partner (MoniCloud Inc.). Artifacts available: vendor contract excerpt, SOC 2 Type II for the vendor (if public), agent deployment manifests, and data flow diagram. We'll include the vendor list in the playbook appendix.

Action items and timeline (confirmed):
- 2028-05-18 10:00 PT: 30-minute sync (Jasmine/Neha/Karthik + Daniel) — calendar invite to follow.
- By 2028-05-22 EOD: initial evidence index and playbook v1 delivered to s3://redwood-evidence/stellarus/STL-2028/.
- By 2028-05-24 EOD: SOC 2 artifacts + key provenance PDF packaged for review.

Delivery mechanics: we'll stage artifacts to the S3 path above and provide a signed, time-limited download link when the bundle is ready. We'll also post a CSV index mapping SIG control IDs -> artifact filenames.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer — Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
